_comment: I0 provider playbook (schema: app/domain/playbook.py). Public facts only, every claim sourced. Non-custodial: Uniswap cannot freeze, hold or return funds. Uniswap Labs' interface screens connected wallets and blocks those tied to hacked or stolen funds, but the block is interface-only. Never propose a freeze here: use the swap logs to follow the output token to the next custodian or issuer.
notes: A screened (blocked) address can still hold and receive assets and can call the protocol contracts directly; only state-changing actions in the Uniswap Labs interface are disabled. Screening uses third-party blockchain analytics (TRM Labs). The privacy policy says it logs the connected wallet's public address and does not collect names or IP addresses, so little off-chain data exists to disclose. If the output was USDT or USDC, the issuer is the freeze route.

paths.notes: At most an interface block of the addresses holding stolen funds: it traps nothing. Low priority: spend the time on the next custodian or issuer.

instrument.notes: The policy shares data in the course of litigation or regulatory proceedings; the exact clause was not readable.

paths.notes: Only the logged wallet addresses and interface usage exist; no accounts, names or IP addresses (Apr 2024 policy version).
